name: OpenMM/CUDA, CHARMM36m + TIP3P, 2 fs without HMR, 310 K

rationale.forcefield: CHARMM36m has native templates for ATP/ADP/MG/CAL; ff14SB does not. A target whose nucleotide cofactor is mandatory cannot use the ff14SB protocol: a run that silently drops the nucleotide has lost the site.
rationale.temperature: 310 K rather than 300 K: in F-actin the phalloidin site opens only in rare fluctuations (Voth 2025), and 300 K undersamples the event of interest.
rationale.timestep: 2 fs with constraints and no HMR: there is no F-actin study validating HMR at 4 fs. A deliberately conservative choice.
rationale.divergence: This diverges from md_ff14sb_hmr_300k for a scientific reason, not by oversight. The two protocols coexist; neither corrects the other.

notes: Protocol for a target whose nucleotide cofactor is mandatory. Not exercised by the example campaigns -- it is here as the second protocol, so that choosing one is an explicit decision rather than a default nobody looked at.
literature: Huang et al. 2017 (CHARMM36m); Voth 2025 (F-actin, site opening).
